title: Your first Jest test
summary: Jest runs a test function and reports whether its checks pass. expect gives the actual value; a matcher states the expected result.
introduction: Jest runs a test function and reports whether its checks pass. expect gives the actual value; a matcher states the expected result. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Jest runs a test function and reports whether its checks pass. expect gives the actual value; a matcher states the expected result.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: These are test-file examples for a local project with Jest installed. They do not run in this site's plain JavaScript sandbox. Use the official setup guide with a teacher if needed.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Jest. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("adds two prices", () => { expect(2 + 3).toBe(5); });
blocks.title: Your first Jest test

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the expected value to 6 and read the failure.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Save test code in a test file matched by your local Jest setup.
For more detail later, use this [Jest further reading](https://jestjs.io/docs/getting-started).
